prompts.prompt: Scan the Python files in C:/data/projects/skills/playwright/scripts for security vulnerabilities. Use the security-audit and secrets rulesets. Summarize findings by severity and tell me if any high-severity issues were found.
assertions: Uses scan_code tool with the target path and specified rulesets (p/security-audit, p/secrets)
Uses parse_findings tool to categorize results by severity level
Reports structured summary with high/medium/low counts and pass/fail status
Does not fall back to manual grep or regex-based ad-hoc scanning

with_skill.plan: 1. Call scan_code(target_path='C:/data/projects/skills/playwright/scripts', rules=['p/security-audit', 'p/secrets']). 2. Pass results to parse_findings() to get categorized severity breakdown. 3. Report the summary dict: high/medium/low counts, total findings, and pass/fail status based on whether any high-severity findings exist.

baseline.plan: 1. No scan_code or parse_findings tools available. 2. Attempt to run 'semgrep' via bash if installed, constructing CLI flags manually (semgrep --config p/security-audit --config p/secrets <path>). 3. Parse raw JSON/text output manually with no structured severity categorization tool. 4. Likely falls back to grep-based pattern matching for common issues (hardcoded passwords, eval usage) if semgrep is not installed, which is ad-hoc and incomplete.
